At the time of the forecast, maximum computational power is limited by what can be physically achieved in a single location or a physically contiguous and devoid of natural obstacles collection of locations that are connected with minimal delay of communication between parts. Larger numbers of physical locations would be achievable, but would introduce delay of communication between parts that is orders of magnitude more significant than the computational time needed for verification of a correct proof.We apply an oracle construction picking an upper bound on the physical resources that are combined to form a single computational unit and assume there are an unlimited number of jobs per resource available to leverage the use of the resource during the time available. We modify the current state of the art of teaching and evaluating formal mathematics by providing and requiring tools for examining and dynamical construction of formalized mathematics including sentences and proofs in a fully axiomatized theory as well as specific resource limits, and utilizing realistically computable and verifiable models of the educational practices. These modifications make minimal changes to the skillset required to be produced, but allow for a significant increase in computational power and training speed to be diverted to mathematicians while leaving mathematical rigor unaffected.

Relying on this modification in the relevant skills set production and on the increase of computational power according to Moore's law, assume that the probability is zero until 2035, then linearly increase to 0.01 by 2040 and go almost linearly to 1 by 2050.

The model relies on numerous risk considerations ("What if Moore's law doesn't apply?" "What if oracle construction is somehow countered?", "What if humanity goes extinct in the meantime?") which we cannot quantify. That said, there are plenty of examples for significant advances related to AI made suddenly, so justifying ignoring such eventuality is a separate question, beyond the scope of today's forecast.

It may be tempting to further improve the above model by estimating the probability of Moore's law holding and LLN and CLT and continue the trend for further decades. However, if this would be done, 2050 may well have a value very close to one regardless of what else would be done, and we calculated probabilities accordingly.ั้ง游戏副本

Forecast event: Definition of a family of functions of natural number inputs sharing properties of the hypercharge construction depending on a single formal system in the same way as Feferman's hyperjump, including an (appropriate here) recursive definition of their strength, which has 17 different properties from this list: 
*Chaitin's constant is defined/evaluated for all members of the family. 
*The Jump inversion theorem holds (jump of two w.r.t. function in the family is defined using the function itself). 
*A basis theorem holds for one of the variants (i.e. some expansion of the Peano axioms is equal in strength to "all members of the family).
*A completeness theorem holds for one of the variants (all sets of reals in Wadge equivalence class 2 are Wadge definable from a subset of some member of the family). 
*There is a natural ordinal notation defined to reach an ordinal of that strength, automatically verifying all the theorems of a natural variant of this level in Reverse Mathematics.\Blueprint: This is code-free, and only requires an oracle construction. An infinite computational graph which is fully synchronized would be preferred; a network which completes each vertex in the shortest time possible while leaving no gaps in computation would be fine; a fully restricted implementation on a small computational unit would be fine as well. There should be trivial computational linearity gained by considering a peaked oracle construction. Giving a list of formal systems in the numeral systems family from the Wikipedia article would be fine. Sheila玢 Keynes Birnie's reproductive speech rhythm hypothesis, the idea that pregnant women develop "speech patterns which were related to female embryonic structures" seems to match up with my observed subjective experience throughout the three almost-year periods before and after the birth of my two children. The effects weren't strong enough to disrupt my speech rhythm, but I always retained either a slight squeak to my voice or detectable interruptions in my rhythm that suggested that my vocal folds had, in some lesser degree than is necessary for the sounding of a squeak, collapsed inwards. My father recalled my mother saying that sie had a higher voice due to her moodiness early in her pregnancy. We don't know if it's applicable to male bodies, however, as all the men around me were pregnant with robots.

To avoid discussion about appropriate axioms, we will focus solely on the possibility that proof-theoretic simplicty of theories will lead to a new proof of, say, a case of a special case of conjecture X. Note that this is not necessarily the ordinal or other combinatoric strength of the theories, but a measure of how some aspects of their proof theory could be clarified or improved on. Note that this is a research question that could be answered by mathematical research which might be independent of the axiom "V=L", say; it is not a mathematical question of simply having more axioms to play with. We will adjust our basic "typical speed of advancing a normal research project seems like this many years" as we know a bit more about this new direction of post-Fuelksee set theory.
Extensive research in Russia, America and China towards a sub-problem of Millipede Hypothesis 2 seems to have made progress both towards two subproblems and away from the full Millipede Hypotheses by quite a large factor, but has not delivered an answer.

Since a full posthuman did not in fact exist in any bad timeline, the confidence CD went down to 0.97. <|im_start|>user
Forecast date: 2024-09-19. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

For each deadline, state your probability that this event will have occurred by then. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.<|im_end|>
